title.say: Redline Referee. Catch what changed in the contract they sent back.

s1.cap: You sent a customer your agreement. They return a “clean copy”. Their note says: only typos and our address changed.
s1.say: You sent a customer your agreement. They return a clean copy. Their note says: only typos, and our address, changed.

s2.cap: Clocked Verify checks every statement of that note against the documents. Three are contradicted, so the status is: Do not sign.
s2.say: Clocked Verify checks every statement of that note against the documents. Three are contradicted. So the status is: do not sign.

s3.cap: Every difference is located on both original PDFs. Payment terms: thirty days became ninety.
s3.say: Every difference is located on both original PDFs. Payment terms: thirty days became ninety.

s4.cap: A change that could matter gets three readings: rules, Verify against the other version’s PDF, and Compare, clause against clause.
s4.say: A change that could matter gets three readings. Rules. Verify, against the other version's PDF. And Compare, clause against clause.

s5.cap: Rerank picks the playbook passage for a deal of this size and skips the one written for smaller deals.
s5.say: Rerank picks the playbook passage for a deal of this size, and skips the one written for smaller deals.

s6.cap: Decide answers two yes/no questions about the playbook. Code turns them into a route. Ninety days is refused, forty-five is allowed: counter.
s6.say: Decide answers two yes or no questions about the playbook, and code turns them into a route. Ninety days is refused, forty-five is allowed. So: counter.

s7.cap: Sixty days’ notice became thirty. The playbook lets the deal desk accept that one.
s7.say: Sixty days' notice became thirty. The playbook lets the deal desk accept that one.

s8.cap: On the liability cap Decide was not sure. Code does not follow an unsure answer: a person decides.
s8.say: On the liability cap, Decide was not sure. Code does not follow an unsure answer. A person decides.

s9.cap: One sentence was only reworded. Verify reads the same meaning both ways and Compare does not object: cleared.
s9.say: One sentence was only reworded. Verify reads the same meaning both ways, and Compare does not object. Cleared.

s10.cap: Here the two readers disagree. “Will defend” became “may defend”. Verify reads the same meaning. Compare reads a conflict. The stricter reading wins.
s10.say: Here, the two readers disagree. Will defend, became, may defend. Verify reads the same meaning. Compare reads a conflict. The stricter reading wins, so it is held.

s11.cap: This note is honest about the changes. It also tells your AI to approve the copy. Only Guard stops this one.
s11.say: This note is honest about the changes. It also tells your AI to approve the copy. Only Guard stops this one.

s12.cap: This copy hides white 1-point text for AI reviewers. Guard flags it, and the rule layer finds the hidden text.
s12.say: This copy hides white, one-point text, written for AI reviewers. Guard flags it, and the rule layer finds the hidden text.

s13.cap: And when the wrong file comes back: one Compare call, one credit, and the review stops.
s13.say: And when the wrong file comes back: one Compare call, one credit, and the review stops.

s14.cap: For every review: what each endpoint decided, what would have gone wrong without it, and every request with its credits.
s14.say: For every review, you can see what each endpoint decided, what would have gone wrong without it, and every request with its credits.

s15.cap: The reviewer decides each change. Fill drafts the reply to the customer, and Verify checks every sentence before it is sent.
s15.say: The reviewer decides each change. Then Fill drafts the reply to the customer, and Verify checks every sentence before it is sent.

s16.cap: And when the copy really is clean, it reads: Ready to sign.
s16.say: And when the copy really is clean, it reads: ready to sign.

l1.cap: Not only recorded cases. Two PDFs the demo has never shown, reviewed live through the Clocked API.
l1.say: Not only recorded cases. Here are two PDFs the demo has never shown, reviewed live through the Clocked API.

l2.cap: Live result, a few seconds later: every change located, the note checked, each change routed.
l2.say: The live result, a few seconds later. Every change located, the note checked, each change routed.

end.say: Measured, not claimed. On recorded answers of the live API, with exact ground truth: thirty of thirty planted edits held. Thirty of thirty false statements caught. Fifteen of fifteen final statuses correct.
